Refactor int hash map into a generic java.util.Map with a JMH harness

Replaces the original single-file int->int open-addressing hash map with a
modular, generic, well-tested implementation.

Correctness fixes over the original:
- Auto-resizing table; the fixed capacity-20 version looped forever once full.
- Negative keys no longer crash (spread hash + power-of-two bit-mask instead of
  a modulo that could go negative).
- Removed the -1 sentinel that was overloaded as both tombstone key and
  "not found" value, so any key/value is now legal.
- Fixed a duplicate-key bug when reinserting into a reclaimed tombstone slot.

Design:
- Generic OpenAddressingHashMap<K, V> implementing java.util.Map via AbstractMap,
  with O(1) overrides of the hot path (get/put/remove/containsKey/size/clear) so
  it never falls back to AbstractMap's O(n) defaults.
- Live, fail-fast entrySet/keySet/values views with write-through and iterator
  removal; value-based equals/hashCode per the Map contract.
- Struct-of-arrays storage (parallel keys/values arrays) removing the per-entry
  node object and its indirection.
- Tombstone deletion with reclamation on insert and clearing on resize.

Tooling and docs:
- Demo separated from the data structure.
- Dependency-free self-checking test suite (63 checks), including a differential
  test against java.util.HashMap and cross-Map interoperability.
- JMH benchmark harness comparing against java.util.HashMap: a self-contained
  benchmarks/run.sh (no build tool required) and a Maven pom.xml.
- README documenting the design, trade-offs, and honest benchmark findings
  (this implementation is competitive but not a uniform win over the JDK map).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
